extracted.intended_audience: ship captains, pilots, and officers of a royal Spanish expedition (early 17th century)
extracted.subtask_description: Operational and disciplinary instructions for captains and admirals conducting a royal discovery voyage: navigation plans, watchkeeping, discipline, provisioning, charting/reporting, and rules for contact with natives and ports. These are orders to be followed in steering, signalling, and maintaining the ship and crew.

rubrics_metrics.name: Maintain Christian, political, and military discipline
rubrics_metrics.description: I specially charge the said Admiral that he is to maintain Christian, political, and military discipline among the men of his ship.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Discipline covers religious observance, obedience to officers, and military order; it is a general duty placed on the Admiral and enforced through the other specific rules (punishments, rituals, respect for command).

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibit blasphemy and punish offenders
rubrics_metrics.description: He is to see that they do not curse nor blaspheme... and if perchance there are some so wicked as to dare to utter such blasphemies, he is to punish them severely and rigorously as their crimes deserve.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Blasphemers forfeit their ration for the day (or next day if already eaten); first offence may be pardoned, repeated offences may lead to irons or fines 'for the benefit of souls in purgatory'; a copy of this chapter is to be nailed to the ship's main mast as notice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Forbid gambling with cards or dice
rubrics_metrics.description: He is to charge him not to consent to any playings with dice or cards... and if by chance there should be any playing cards found in his ship, or dice (except for playing at backgammon), he is to throw them overboard...
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Gambling is considered prejudicial to the voyage; games causing disputes are to be thrown overboard to avoid mischief.

rubrics_metrics.name: Daily communal prayers and litany of Our Lady of Loreto
rubrics_metrics.description: He is to take great care that every day, in the afternoon, all the people go on their knees before an altar... and that the Litany of Our Lady of Loreto is recited, praying for her favour and intercession.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Religious observance is institutionalized as daily practice to seek divine guidance and success; it is part of voyage discipline and morale.

rubrics_metrics.name: Penalties for taking God's name in vain
rubrics_metrics.description: He forbids any one from taking God's name in vain, the person so offending forfeiting his ration for that day, and if he has already had it, for the next day... if he repents first time may be pardoned, for the second, third... he may be put in irons, or fined.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provides escalating punishments and mandates that punishment may not be remitted; even messmates who feed the offender suffer the same ration penalty.

rubrics_metrics.name: Forbid disrespect toward the royal person and service
rubrics_metrics.description: He is to be very vigilant in preventing free or disrespectful words being spoken of the royal person or his service: and those who so offend are to be punished promptly and with rigour.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Protects royal authority aboard ship; punishments should be justified and applied promptly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Treat crew kindly, honor officers, and govern without cruelty
rubrics_metrics.description: He is to take care and use much diligence in treating kindly and lovingly all the people under his charge, and to honour and maintain each one of his officers in the posts they occupy... remembering how worthy of esteem that Captain is who, without the use of knife or other rigour, governs his people in peace.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Leadership should prefer kindness and firm governance over cruelty; maintain mutual respect among officers to keep crew content and loyal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Master to prevent spoilage and wastage of provisions
rubrics_metrics.description: He is to look after the Master of the Ship with vigilance, who is to see that the provisions do not turn bad and are not wasted; and that those respecting which there is a suspicion that they may turn bad are used first.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Active management of stores to avoid spoilage and to prioritize use of suspect provisions early.

rubrics_metrics.name: Daily rations specified
rubrics_metrics.description: The ration to be served out each day to each person... is 1 1/2 lbs. of biscuit, 1 lb. of meat, 2 oz. of bacon, 1 oz. of pulses, half a gallon of water for drinking... On fish days the ration is to be one fish... If there is no fish, 4 oz. of cheese is to be substituted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explicit food and water allowances for voyage duration; allowance for fish days and substitutions; extras to be managed to prevent complaints and conserve for long voyage.

rubrics_metrics.name: Follow Capitana's course and navigation contingency plan
rubrics_metrics.description: He is to be very diligent... in following the Capitana ship, which will shape a W.S.W. course until the latitude of 30° is reached; and when that is reached and no land has been seen, the course will be altered to N.W. until the latitude of 10° 15'... and if no land has yet been found, a course will be followed on that parallel to the west, in search of the island of Santa Cruz.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Detailed routing and waypoint protocol; later instructions for anchoring in bay of Graciosa at 10°, waiting three months for other ships, and marking/burying notices if separated; if alone, steering instructions (S.W. to 20°, then N.W. to 4°, then west to seek New Guinea then Manila).

rubrics_metrics.name: Protocol if ships separate: mark site and bury narrative
rubrics_metrics.description: The Captain who arrives first in this port... is to anchor there, and wait there three months for the other two ships. When together, a resolution will be taken... If by chance the other ships do not arrive, the Captain, before he departs, is to raise a cross, and at the foot of it, or of the nearest tree, he is to make a sign on the trunk, to be understood by him who next arrives, and to bury a jar with the mouth closed with tar, and containing a narrative of all that has happened and of his intentions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Standardized signaling and record-keeping practice to preserve information for other ships and for the Crown.

rubrics_metrics.name: Take celestial observations frequently and correct for leeway and variation
rubrics_metrics.description: He is to be diligent in taking the sun daily, and at night the star Crucero... that he may know his latitude and plot it on his chart, making allowances for lee-way... and for the variation of the needle; and for greater accuracy, he shall take care to correct it by the sun, or by a known star when on the meridian.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Mandates regular latitude determination and correction procedures for accurate navigation and charting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Keep detailed log of daily voyages and environmental signs
rubrics_metrics.description: He is also to be careful to note the number of leagues made by the ship each day, the winds and the changes, the showers, currents, flights of birds, shoals of fishes, and signs of land, with its appearance when sighted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Daily recording of many voyage data points to support navigation, charting, and later reporting to the King.

rubrics_metrics.name: Chart islands and continental features with lat/long and descriptors
rubrics_metrics.description: Also, he is to note the islands, whether inhabited or uninhabited, and place them on the chart in their latitude, longitude, and form. If it is continental land, he is to do the same as regards ports, capes, anchorages, and all other features; writing descriptions of the positions of each feature...
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Instructions for cartographic notation (dots for sand, crosses for rocks) and to record resources (wood, water), hazards (rocks, reefs), and anchorages for Crown records.

rubrics_metrics.name: Record inhabitants' physical and cultural details
rubrics_metrics.description: Besides these details, the colour, shape, features, and dress of the inhabitants are to be noted, their food, arms, boats, behaviour, and government and religion; so that a full and detailed account can be given to the King...
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ethnographic and material description requirements intended for strategic and missionary purposes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Daily visits to the Capitana and customary protocol
rubrics_metrics.description: Every day he will come up to this Capitana, as is the custom, to give his respects and wish for a good voyage; and to ask for the word, which will be answered and given in the customary way.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Maintains chain of command, communication, and ceremonial respect among ships of the fleet.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rigorous lookout schedules and personal accountability
rubrics_metrics.description: He is to take care that, at sunrise and sunset, and oftener if it seems desirable, two men go to the masthead to look out over all parts of the horizon; and at night the sentries are to be doubled, one being on the bowsprit... The rounds and over-rounds are to be gone by him in person, and when he is not able, he is to delegate the duty to others in whom he has confidence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sentries must be punctual; captain personally inspects rounds or delegates; punish those found sleeping or negligent; in taking in sail during threatening weather there must be no negligence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Signal procedures for course changes, land, and requests
rubrics_metrics.description: When the Capitana puts out a flag from the main topmast, it is a signal to the pilots for the ships to close... If the Capitana should alter course during the night, a gun will be fired; if it is desired to give notice that land is sighted, or that there are rocks, two guns will be fired... By day use flags; by night two lights besides the stern lantern as a signal that help is needed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Standardized visual and auditory signals with required repetition by other ships to confirm understanding.

rubrics_metrics.name: Strict fire precautions below decks
rubrics_metrics.description: Great precautions are to be taken against fire. There is to be no lighted candle nor other fire between decks, except within a lantern in charge of a man to watch it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Designate a trusted watchman for any lanterns below decks; prevent accidental fires which threaten ships and stores.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prevent waste and fraud of royal stores
rubrics_metrics.description: Much care is to be taken that there is no waste in cord, powder, or balls; and attention is to be given to all the royal stores that there may be no fraud whatever in their expenditure.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Active oversight of military and royal supplies to conserve resources and prevent embezzlement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sound and heave-to when wind and sea suddenly cease at night
rubrics_metrics.description: If there is both wind and sea, and both suddenly cease, being night time, heave to and sound, and keep a good look-out, as the cause may be the interposition of land close to.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Immediate precautionary sounding and lookout when unusual calm occurs to avoid unexpected grounding.

rubrics_metrics.name: Take soundings when puffs/flaws or unusual ship motion occur at night
rubrics_metrics.description: If there are puffs and flaws of wind besides the wind that fills the sails, or the ship raises her head and stern as if she was being pushed, it being night time, take soundings, for she may be very near the land or rocks, where the sea breaks and sends back the surf.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use soundings proactively to detect proximity to hidden shoals or reefs during anomalous sea conditions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Heave-to and sound on certain atmospheric/visual signs of land
rubrics_metrics.description: If the sky being clear, the sun, moon, and stars come out and are higher than the horizon, it is a certain sign of land; at night heave to and sound, at daytime look out for it. If thick mists ahead which do not move away, or a fixed line, or a damp fog, heave to and sound... If certain flashes with little lights are seen ahead, accompanied by thunder... heave to and sound.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Enumerates environmental indicators (celestial heights, persistent mists, luminous flashes with thunder) that require immediate sounding and increased caution.

rubrics_metrics.name: Respond to dry gusts, greasy sea, and floating debris as signs of land
rubrics_metrics.description: If in spite of the wind that is blowing there come dry gusts from another quarter, or with rain or hail, it is a sign of land being near... If the sea appears greasy, with leaves of trees, grass, herbs, wood, branches, palm nuts, and other things which the waves carry from the shores... it is a sign of land being near...
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Interpretation of surface debris and anomalous winds as land proximity cues; act accordingly (heave to, sound, lookout).

rubrics_metrics.name: Use wildlife and water colour as indicators of land and bottom type
rubrics_metrics.description: If there are currents it is better when they are strong, or there are shoals of small fishes... or patches of camarones, sea snakes, seals, turtles, much bad water, or some land birds, take care, for the ship will be very near the land... If patches of brown water are seen on the sea, it is a sign that there are rocks near the surface; if the patches are white, it is a sign of a sandy bottom... a black patch is a sign of ooze and mud; and a green patch points to a bottom covered with weeds.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Observe birds (boobies, petrels, piqueros, gulls, etc.) and their timing to infer distance to land; adjust vigilance and take soundings based on water colour and wildlife cues.

rubrics_metrics.name: Maintain vigilance after anchoring; guard against native sabotage
rubrics_metrics.description: After anchoring in any port, a careful look-out should be kept both by day and night, for the natives are great swimmers and divers, and might wedge up the rudder, cut the hawsers, or set fire to the ship. For this reason it is well, in places where there is cause for suspicion, to have a guard in the boat at night over the buoys, or at least to visit them many times.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Mandates night boat guard over buoys or repeated inspections to prevent underwater sabotage and fires.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limit and control number of natives aboard
rubrics_metrics.description: Take care not to allow so many natives on board the ship as would be able to overpower the crew; and even when they are few, great evil may come to them as well as to us, from ignorance of our arms; whence may arise a commencement of war, and a faithful peace may never then be made.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Restrict boarding to safe numbers to prevent being overwhelmed and to avoid accidental escalation to conflict due to unfamiliarity with weapons.

rubrics_metrics.name: Make landings by day, in level clear places, with precautions against ambush
rubrics_metrics.description: In effecting a landing, it should always be by day, and never at night. The landing-place should be level and clear of woods, or at least as well situated... sending dogs in front to discover ambushes, with arms ready, marching together and in order, and entering passes with caution.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use reconnaissance (dogs), disciplined formation, and choose terrain carefully because natives may conceal themselves behind rocks/trees or lie flat in grass.

rubrics_metrics.name: Keep important natives as hostages but treat them well and give presents
rubrics_metrics.description: Take notice that, if it is possible, chiefs or other natives who appear to be of consequence, should be kept in the ship as hostages, but well treated and given presents of things that they seem to like most. The same course should be followed on shore, when the natives seek intercourse and conversation with us.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use hostage-taking of leaders as a security strategy combined with respectful treatment and gift-giving to facilitate peaceful relations and negotiation.
